text: We may be small on the map, but we sit right at the crossroads of the world – by land, by air, by sea and increasingly, by data and technology.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: In transport, if you want to stay relevant, you cannot afford to miss the boat.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: If we are not moving forward, we risk being left at the platform.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: In this increasingly unpredictable world, the strength of Singapore's transport sector and its diversity of interconnectedness to the rest of the world is not only an economic priority but also one of national security.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore's success today as a global transport hub did not happen by chance.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: It is the decades of hard work of our businesses, the many Singaporean workers and public servants across the transport sector.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: A world-class transport hub needs a world-class workforce.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: We must do our best to create these jobs and empower Singaporeans to excel in them.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: To this, I will speak on three key areas.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: First, how our AI strategy is integral to creating good jobs in the transport sector.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: And third, matching international connectivity with local transport infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: As the transport sector develops, we need to prepare a workforce that will be able to meet the needs of the future.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: To get there, I would like to ask how the Government is preparing our workforce for this transformation.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: AI has taken centrestage over the past few years.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: As a country, we have been doing a lot to develop a workforce with sufficient tech professionals, including data scientists, developers and product managers, as well as a larger general workforce that is comfortable with using AI in their domain.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) is undertaking to ensure we engage in frontier research and to expand our education institutions' capacity to train AI talent.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Tech giants are not the only ones who need tech talent.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I call on the Government to ensure our upskilling efforts and AI proficiencies are spread across industries.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: One of the things I value about the transport sector is the wide range of talent it requires: we need brilliant AI scientists to design and maintain the cutting-edge model that will transform the industry as well as skilled technicians on the ground.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Not all these talents are best developed through university education.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Our polytechnics and Institutes of Technical Education (ITEs) will play a crucial role in supplying the workforce of the future.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I encourage the Ministry to broker partnerships between our institutes of higher learning and industry partners to develop and update relevant courses in the present, design programmes that will meet future needs, develop scholarships and internship programmes to draw in talent in advance, and design opportunities for mid-career upgrading and career transition.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The transport sector must transform quickly to stay relevant and our workforce will need to retrain, readjust and in some cases, relearn.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Remaining competitive and creating good jobs for our residents requires constant change.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: But as we push ahead, we must remind one another that compassion must prevail in our society.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Those who helped build this sector must not be left behind.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Even as we press on to be world-leading, we must ensure change is managed with people at its heart.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: As we adopt AI, these technologies should empower our workforce and not simply replace it.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Our workers should be active partners in this transformation – equipped, involved and given the confidence to experiment with new technologies rather than fear being displaced.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I now turn to the balance between decarbonisation and energy resilience.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Recent events in the Middle East have reminded us that global energy supply chains remain vulnerable to geopolitical shocks.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Even as countries decarbonise and electrify, many economies will continue, for some time, to depend on reliable supplies of conventional fuels, such as diesel and jet fuel, particularly for aviation, heavy transport and resilience needs.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: For Singapore to remain a leading maritime and global aviation hub, we must recognise this reality.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Beyond their economic contribution, they anchor Singapore's contribution and position in global energy supply chains, support industries that rely on refined fuel products, and preserve capabilities and expertise that have been built over decades.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: These strategic considerations should form part of any long-term plans for Jurong Island refineries.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: To pursue decarbonisation while maintaining our transport sector's economic competitiveness is a precarious balancing act.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: While it is important for us to take tangible steps towards lowering our emissions and taking the measured approach towards increasing the mandated proportion of sustainable aviation fuel blend, this should proceed with caution.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: While we currently have a competitive advantage, which would offset these additional costs, we should and must never take our existing competitive advantage for granted.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: So, I urge MOT to take calibrated steps in future on mandatory sustainable aviation fuel blend rates.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The best way for us to maintain our long-term competitive advantage in the transport sector is to proactively shape the standards of the industry.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The Technical Reference 68 is one good start.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: We must continue to play that strategic role of shaping the international standards on safety, ethics and security in the usage of autonomous technologies and AI in this industry.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, I believe our intent to be a global transport hub is not just to create good jobs and pursue economic growth.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: All these are important, but we also want to be able to deliver to Singaporeans connectivity that improves their lived experiences.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: So, therefore, upstream planning, transport planning is critical to avoid bottlenecks that will be difficult to solve once residents move in.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I am grateful to have started early conversations with key agencies, including LTA, on plans for the local transport network or upgrades for Khatib MRT.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: For residents, it is often the small improvements that make the biggest difference.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: More accessible pathways and well-planned transport flow can make everyday journeys safer and easier.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I look forward to working closely with the Ministry, LTA, and our community partners and our residents to plan ahead, address the needs early, deliver practical improvements that will serve Chencharu well for years to come.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, I support this Motion.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore's status as a globally connected hub for aviation, maritime and logistics did not come easily, and we must never take it for granted.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: A world-class transport hub requires a world-class workforce.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: We must create as many of these jobs as possible and equip Singaporeans with the capabilities to fill them.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: More importantly, what plans do we have to train, attract and retain talent so as to ensure that Singapore continues to maintain its edge?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: We also aspire to achieve genuine connectivity in every sense – one that enhances the lived experience of the Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: In Nee Soon South, the Chencharu area is set to see around 10,000 new homes built by 2040.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: This means that over the next 15 years, approximately 30,000 new residents are expected to move in at an average of around 2,000 per year.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Early planning is essential to prevent transport bottlenecks that would be difficult to resolve once the residents have already moved in.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad to have been able to engage early with the key agencies, such as LTA, to begin preliminary discussions on expanding the transport networks in Nee Soon South or upgrading Khatib MRT station.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: For residents, it is often these small improvements that make the greatest difference.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Better pedestrian access and well-planned transport connections can make daily commutes safer and more convenient.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I look forward to continuing to work with MOT, LTA and our community partners. : Mr Deputy Speaker, I look to the future of our transport sector with optimism.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: A world-class transport sector gives our residents more than convenience.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: It connects them seamlessly across Singapore and opens the door to the world for leisure, education, business and work.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Because when Singapore moves well, the world moves with us.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Once upon a time, I had a power pressure craft licence, a pilot licence and, of course, a driving licence.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But of course, it piqued my interest in mobility solutions and so, I spent quite a bit of time working in these sectors.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: For the Minister for Transport's information, I got my flying licence on my very first test but driving cost me five tests.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Which means our road traffic regulations are very tight.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The transportation or mobility sector is a very important area or sector or industry for Singapore as a sea hub, air hub.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: And so, I would like to focus on innovations and to support the entrepreneurs of deep tech ventures, especially, right now, where with the advance of AI, autonomous technology, drones, this has become a fertile field for us to create many possibilities for our industries in the mobility sector.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But there are actually issues that we face.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I note that the wing-in-ground (WIG) craft brought in by ST Engineering known as the "air fish" that floats above the surface of the water.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But however, it takes quite a bit of time.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: We know that the craft existed for many, many years, but it has been tested overseas and then after that, once they are ready and it will be brought back to Singapore.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I like to compare this against two aerospace engineers, who are from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, America, and they are aerospace engineers trained in drones and trained in AVs, and they founded this company called Regent Craft, founded in 2020.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I think the imaginations and possibilities in the maritime and mobility industries or transportation industry for our people are infinite.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: And therefore, we really have to enable them to go and find these possibilities.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The issue really is that in Singapore, confined environment especially air and sea, it is very difficult for us to trial or pilot anything that is moving.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Well, it is for good reason, risk management and also, not to affect our normal operations.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, localised sandboxes both for sea, land and air; and then regional sandboxes so that trials for such craft, which needs longer distance, more complex operations can be done.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I note that in the Nanyang Technological University when they are developing these flying cars, in Singapore, they do trials, they are tethered.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But when they need to do free-flying, it was reported that they go to Germany.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Indonesia also has a master plan for the other alternative means for low altitude economy called advanced air mobility and therefore, it is an opportunity for us to partner with them to allow or partner such that our companies can go there and do longer-distance flight trials or these testings.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I would also want to commend the initiatives, the innovations, for example, MPA, which is on PIER71, which creates a lot of innovations.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I think that we should consolidate all these into maybe an agency for innovation within MOT from air, sea and land; and then put in aggressive funding and piloting such that this could be a pillar for our economy in the future.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It is about Singapore's long-term relevancy in the global economy.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: There is an old saying: ships do not sail because the sea is calm; they sail because they are built to weather the storm.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Singapore became a leading aviation, maritime and logistic hub not because geography favoured us but because we transform opportunity into excellency through vision, trusted institution and the determination of our people.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Businesses are placing greater emphasis not only on efficiency, but also resilience, sustainability and trust.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The question before us is simple: how do we ensure companies continue to choose Singapore not just to move goods but to invest, manage regional operations and create high value jobs?

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: When we discuss strengthening Singapore as a global transport hub, we naturally think about airports, ports and infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Our freight forwarders, customs brokers, engineering firms, logistics technology companies and service providers are the backbone of our transport ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Every MNC was once a small business with a big ambition.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: If Singapore is to remain competitive, we must help today's SMEs become tomorrow's regional champions.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Tuas Port is becoming one of the world's largest automated ports.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: But merging our physical and digital infrastructure must include our SMEs and not just our ports and terminals.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The challenge for many SMEs is not buying technology.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It is knowing which solutions to adopt, integrating them into operations, training employees and generating real business value.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Grants are important, but they are only the starting point.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Second, we should continue helping our SMEs internationalise with confidence.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Many businesses need support to navigate overseas regulations, identify reliable partners and understand emerging markets.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Every Singapore enterprise that successfully expands overseas strengthens our economic resilience and reinforces Singapore's position as an international global business hub.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: AI can recommend routes, but people make judgement calls.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: AI can automate processes, but people manage exceptions, build relations and create trust.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: So, the future workforce needs not only digital skills but also operational judgement, communication and problem-solving.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Low-carbon shipping, green warehousing and sustainable supply chains are no longer optional.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Increasingly, they determine whether companies win or lose the contracts.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Helping SMEs adopt greener technologies is therefore not only an environmental priority but also an economic necessity.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Above all, businesses know that when Singapore makes a commitment, we deliver; and that reputation is priceless.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Singapore should aim to move from being a transit hub to becoming a decision hub.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: A transit hub is where goods pass through.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: A decision hub is where companies decide how goods move, where they move, how risks are managed and how regional supply chains are coordinated, where they locate their supply chain control towers, procurement centres, digital trade platforms, financing functions and risk management capabilities.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And also, where should they coordinate between air, sea and land logistics.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This is where higher value jobs are created when we are reinforcing Singapore’s position as a global transportation hub.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: That is the next stage of Singapore's competitive advantage.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Imagine a visitor arriving in Singapore in the future.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The flight lands at Changi Airport, immigration clearance is fast and largely automated, luggage is tracked digitally.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The traveller may choose for luggage to be transferred securely to the hotel.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Transport, hotel check-in and payment made be connected more smoothly.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: By the time the visitor reaches the hotel, the luggage may already be there.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: When the visitor reaches the hotel, a human concierge may still welcome him, recommend where to eat, explain what to see, and give the warmth and assurance that technology alone cannot provide.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The future of transport is not only about automation.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It is about how systems, companies and people come together to deliver one trusted experience.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Pharmaceutical companies moving temperature-sensitive medicines through Singapore do not only need air cargo.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It needs cold chain logistics, digital documentation, cybersecurity, insurance warehousing, onwards delivery and risk management.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The customer does not experience this as separate sectors.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The customer experiences them as one Singapore system.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Singapore should not simply be where goods move through.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And this is where everything I have said comes togethe – because a decision hub needs capable local partners around it.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Helping our SMEs upgrade is therefore not simply an SME policy.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: As the NTUC slogan goes, "Every Worker Matters".

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I believe “Every SME Matters” and “Every Family Matters” too.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: As our founding Prime Minister, Mr Lee Kuan Yew, reminded us, "If we do not remain relevant to the world, the world will not remain interested in us." Let us continue helping our enterprises innovate, internationalise and grow.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: When our workers prosper, our economy becomes stronger.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And when our economy remains strong, Singapore's future remains secure.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Singapore of the future should not merely be a place where goods pass through quickly.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It should be a place that creates value, generates knowledge and develops solutions.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Today, advanced technology can be acquired anywhere in the world and modern ports and airports can be built by any country.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: When global enterprises choose Singapore in the future, it will not simply be because of our efficiency.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It will be because they trust that here, they can make important decisions with confidence, manage regional operations and find partners they can rely on.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: In my view, we cannot focus solely on nurturing a handful of successful large enterprises.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: When a local SME is able to enter an international supply chain through innovative solution, the impact goes far beyond its own growth.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: It creates more local jobs, develops more skilled professionals and makes the entire Singapore economy more competitive.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: That is what a truly sustainable model of development looks like.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The competition among global transport hubs in the future will not be fought on speed alone.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Technology can improve efficiency and AI can optimise processes.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: But integrity cannot be auto generated, and reputation cannot be built by algorithms.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: As long as we continue to uphold openness and cooperation, pursue relentless innovation, develop our people and move forward hand-in-hand with businesses and workers, I am confident that Singapore will not only maintain its leading position as a global transport hub, but will also become the most trusted decision-making centre for enterprises worldwide, creating more quality jobs for Singaporeans and lay a stronger foundation for the generations to come. : Mr Deputy Speaker, I support the Motion.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: We think of PSA with the towering cranes at Pasir Panjang, Jurong and Tuas Port.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: We think of the many ships in our waters and the seamless movement of cargo through our logistics network, including our land transport network.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: These are powerful symbols of success for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: A transport hub is only complete because of the people who keep it moving, 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: From the baggage handler working on the tarmac; the technicians ensuring that every vehicle operates safely; the crane operators managing multiple cranes from a control room, the harbour pilot guiding some of the world's largest vessels into our ports; our air traffic controllers and airport crew who ensure the safety of airplanes in and out of Singapore and ensuring people coming through Singapore get the best experience; the seafarer spending months away from home to keep global trade flowing; the logistics planner ensuring that supply chains continue to function, so businesses receive their goods and families receive their parcels.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: These are the men and women who built Singapore's transport hub reputation.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: They kept our transport system moving during COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: They kept global trade flowing through supply chain disruptions.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: They adapted through manpower shortages and global uncertainties.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Today, as we speak of transforming and strengthening Singapore's position as a global transport hub, my question is: how will we bring these people along and what is the future that they see as part of that strong futuristic global hub that we want to be?

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Because, Mr Deputy Speaker, the future of transport should not be something our workers merely adapt to.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: It must be a future they can look forward to.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Looking at our maritime sector, from the early days of the Singapore River to Jurong Port after Independence, to containerisation at Tanjong Pagar, Singapore has never stood still.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Today, our maritime sector is entering another transformation.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore now operates an AI-powered Maritime Digital Twin, integrating real-time information from vessels, weather systems and sensors to optimise traffic and improve safety.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Yard cranes and automated guided vehicles are remotely operated.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: MPA is driving innovation in autonomous vessels and new maritime fuels, while strengthening Singapore's International Maritime Centre.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: And we already see what this means for our workers.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: More than 30 years ago, he began as a yard crane operator at PSA, climbing high into crane cabins every day in physically demanding work.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Today, he is a Senior Quay Crane Specialist, supervising automated operations, mentoring younger colleagues and leading the adoption of new technologies.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: His career did not end because technology arrived.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Likewise, Mr Tan Sin Poh from Jurong Port has spent over two decades developing engineering expertise.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Today, he leads highly complex equipment relocation projects that require precision planning, engineering excellence and close teamwork.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: His experience has become even more valuable in a technologically advanced port.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: These stories remind us that transformation succeeds when workers succeed.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: The same transformation is taking place in aviation.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Behind every redesigned job is a worker who must learn new skills.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Behind every new technology is a worker who must be confident enough to use it.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: And behind every transformation is a family depending on that worker's future.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Our workforce is ageing with low birth rates.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: If we are to remain a leading transport hub, we cannot simply add more workers.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: We must help every worker become more productive, more skilled and able to enjoy longer careers.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: They can allow experienced workers to move into higher-value roles that command better wages and offer greater career progression.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: For our senior workers, technology can extend productive careers instead of shortening them because their bodies can no longer cope with physically demanding work.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: But Mr Deputy Speaker, technology alone does not build trust.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Workers must know that transformation is happening with them, not to them.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: They must know that technology is being deployed to strengthen the Singaporean core.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: And very important, it is to strengthen the Singaporean core: to improve their wages, to improve their welfare, to strengthen their work prospects so that they can stay ahead of the cost curves and provide well for their families.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: That is why I have two calls in support of this Motion.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: First, we must equip and train workers early, with unions involved from the very beginning and we already know that this works with many examples.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: As we build T5, the tripartite model should become the norm.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: CAAS, CAG, SATS, employers and unions must work hand in hand to ensure that every productivity gain is also a gain for workers.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: This is also how we attract young Singaporeans into aviation and the industry.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond competitive salaries, the young people want meaningful careers with opportunities to grow.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, experienced Singaporean workers must remain the heart of our success.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Technology may automate many processes, but it cannot automate the warmth, the professionalism and service excellence that define us, Singapore and as the Singapore experience.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Going forward, the Government should continue to work closely with the NTUC, unions, e2i and the Tripartite Jobs Council to support companies, large and small, to redesign jobs well before disruption takes place.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: All stakeholders should be able to plug into and grow with the vision of a world-class transportation hub.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: It must begin while our workers are still employed.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Second, we must ensure that the good jobs we create are accessible to every Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Where jobs may be affected, companies should work closely with unions to identify impacted workers early, provide sufficient notice and ensure adequate training so workers can transition confidently into new opportunities.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: For our lower-wage workers, technology must become a ladder for upward mobility.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: They should see an upward growth for themselves and their families.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Transformation should narrow opportunity gaps and not widen them.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: And let us not forget persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: The question is not whether transformation will happen.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: The question is whether every Singaporean worker will benefit from it.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Because Singapore's greatest competitive advantage has never been our port.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: Our greatest competitive advantage has always been our people.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: But a highly skilled, adaptable, trusted and resilient Singaporean workforce cannot be replicated easily.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: By investing in workers' capabilities, career progression and resilience, Singapore transforms its workforce from a factor of production into a strategic asset.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: This not only strengthens productivity and service quality but also reinforces Singapore's reputation as a reliable and future-ready global transport hub.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: If we continue investing in our workers, developing their skills and supporting their careers and strengthening the Singaporean core, we will not only reinforce Singapore's position as a global transport hub.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: We will reinforce Singapore's reputation as a nation that succeeds because we never leave our workers behind.

speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
text: And that is what every Singaporean worker can look into the future with confidence, dignity and pride knowing that we have their backs.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: I am also adviser to the Singapore Maritime Officers Union, the Shipbuilding and Marine Engineering Employees Union, and the Singapore Organisation of Seamen.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: This Motion is about reinforcing our position as a global transport hub and my parliamentary colleagues have spoken well.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: But as we discuss ideas and innovations, I think it is worthwhile to ask some fundamental questions: what is a true maritime hub?

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: What makes us a hub in the first place?

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: We top the world too, on vessel arrival tonnage.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: These are impressive statistics and they do matter.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: But they are not what truly distinguishes us.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: It sits at the centre of a deep ecosystem of ancillary and allied maritime industries that draws in and supports one another.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: The depth of this ecosystem is what makes our position as a global maritime hub so resilient, unique and difficult to displace.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: It includes services that are critical to shipping interests but are not always visible to the public, such as bunkering, repair, fleet management, crewing, handling, classification societies, surveyors, insurance brokers and so on.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: That is reinforced by our position as a major oil trading, storage and refining hub.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: We are also a leading ship crewing and marine and trade insurance hub, driven by our excellent global connectivity and banking sector.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Protection and Indemnity (P&I) clubs, financiers, classification societies and fleet managers all cluster here because our legal and financial system is transparent and trusted.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: As you can see, we are no longer just a port where ships call.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: But we have evolved into a place where shipping decisions are made, logistics are arranged, risks are managed, disputes are resolved, contracts concluded and capital deployed.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: This is what distinguishes us as a real maritime hub from just another successful port.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: But what keeps and anchors them here is the trust in the Singapore system.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Strip all the physical infrastructure, and trust is what ultimately underpins Singapore's position as a global maritime hub.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: It has been earned over decades through a capable and far-sighted Government, our independent judiciary and the quality and integrity of our public administration, and of course, our unique tripartite partnership between Government, employers and unions that has kept Singapore free from the industrial disruptions seen elsewhere.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: We may take these things for granted, but they are all factors that global supply chain managers take into account when deciding where to anchor their operations and route their cargo.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Taken together, the message to any global operator is simple.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Singapore is stable and trustworthy, and you can trust Singapore to deliver.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: As many players have observed, recent global disruptions have initiated a border shift in supply chains.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: From focusing on the cheapest and fastest towards the safest and most trusted.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: In other words, the winds have been blowing towards us.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: This is an affirmation of the system we have built.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: We are well positioned to take advantage of that.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: But the challenge is always to stay ahead.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: To do this, we must be clear-eyed about what we face.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: In the sequel to the classic children's novel, Alice in Wonderland, there is a well-known scene where the Red Queen tells Alice that in her country, you must run as fast as you can just to stay where you are.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: The world around us is not standing still.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: For us, to stand still is to fall behind.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Right next door, within sight of our new Tuas Port, the Port of Tanjung Pelapas, backed by global giant APM terminals, is currently expanding.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: And not far away in North Sumatra, Kuala Tanjung is being developed into Indonesia's largest transhipment port and it is backed by DP World, PSA's peer competitor in Dubai.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: They are not out to complement us, but to compete with us.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: World-class expertise has quietly arrived at our doorstep.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong once said that Singapore must always be exceptional just to survive, and I agree.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Larger countries can afford to get some things wrong.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: They have the natural resources and domestic markets to do so.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: For us, the margin for error is exactly zero.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: But our answer to this challenge is implicit in the earlier part of my speech.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Even as we embrace frontier technologies and continue our investments in infrastructure, we must remember that others may embrace the same technologies and build the same world-class infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: They can also hire the world class expertise that they cannot develop themselves.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: But it is the intangibles that we have built that are much harder for others to replicate and follow – the brand name reputation that comes with trusted institutions, a strong Government with good leadership, strong industrial relations, all tied into an ecosystem in which the whole is worth far more than the sum of its parts.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: We must remember that these intangibles were earned over decades and can erode away quickly.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Once lost, they are very difficult to rebuild.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Even the international order is changing before our eyes.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: But for Singapore, certain fundamentals must never change.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But at a deeper level, it is about how Singapore creates value in a changing world.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For decades, Singapore earned its place by connecting the world.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We built one of the world's leading ports, one of the world's best airports and a logistics network that businesses around the world came to rely on.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Although we are a small island with no natural resources, we became relevant because we connected people, markets and opportunities better than almost anyone else.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But every successful strategy must evolve with the world around it.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Technology is changing how goods, services, capital and information move across borders.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The busiest hub is not always the one that creates the most value.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The question is no longer whether goods pass through Singapore.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The question is whether the decisions behind those goods are made in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Increasingly, the greatest value is created long before a container reaches a port or an aircraft leaves the runway.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is created when businesses decide where to source, where to manufacture, where to manage risk and how to respond when disruption strikes.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Those decisions matter more than ever because uncertainty has become a permanent feature of the global economy.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Yesterday, Singapore's role may be to ensure that its cargo moved quickly through our port or airport.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We want its regional operations, supply chain planning and risk management teams to be based here, not because the cargo stays in Singapore, but because the decisions do.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: That is a much stronger position to hold.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is also one that cannot be replicated simply by building another port or another airport.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Because Singapore offers something that has become increasingly valuable in an uncertain world – trust.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It was built patiently over decades through stable institutions, predictable rules, openness to the world and a reputation for keeping our word.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: When global supply chains came under strain, Singapore kept trade moving.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We remained a dependable partner when certainty was in short supply.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Trust is often spoken of as a virtue.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: When businesses decide where to invest, where to establish regional headquarters and where to coordinate operations, they are ultimately deciding where they have confidence in a system.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But infrastructure alone will not determine our future.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Technology will continue to transform aviation, maritime and logistics.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: AI, automation and digital systems will make transport faster, safer and more efficient.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: People decide when resilience is worth the additional cost.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Technology should never be seen as replacing Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It should increase the value that Singaporeans bring.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This also changes how we think about jobs.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Too often, we ask which jobs technology will replace.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Our ambition should not simply be to create more jobs in transport.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It should be to create the jobs where the most important decisions are made.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The jobs that design supply chains rather than merely operate them.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The jobs that coordinate regional operations rather than simply execute instructions.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These are the jobs that will command higher wages because they create greater value.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These are the jobs that global companies will choose to anchor here.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These are the opportunities we must prepare Singaporeans to seize.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We connected the world better than almost anyone else.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: That is why we continue to invest in world-class ports and airports.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But above all, that is why we invest in Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Because infrastructure can be replicated, technology can be acquired, but trust must be earned, judgement must be developed and confidence must be built over time.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If Singapore becomes the place where the world chooses to make its most important transport and supply chain decisions, then goods will continue to flow through our ports and airports.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: More importantly, opportunities will continue to flow to Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: That is how we reinforce Singapore's position as a global transport hub.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Not simply by moving more cargo, but by creating more value.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And not simply for the next decade, but for the next generation.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Every day, hundreds of flights arrive and depart.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Thousands of tonnes of cargo move through our airfreight facilities.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: People, goods and ideas connect Singapore to every corner of the globe.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: But for many of the residents I represent, Changi is something else.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: It is where they report to for work.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: As the MP for Changi and as adviser to the SIA Employees' Union and the Supply Chain Employees' Union, I have had the privilege of speaking to many Singaporeans whose livelihoods depend on our transport ecosystem – cabin crew, aircraft engineers, airport operations staff, freight forwarders, warehouse supervisors and logistics professionals.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: And on behalf of them, I will ask: as our transport hub evolves, will it continue to create good jobs for Singaporeans?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Singapore has never succeeded because of geography alone.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Our success has always come from staying ahead of change.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: If Singapore wants to remain indispensable, we must once again reinvent ourselves.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: First, how do we ensure that strengthening Singapore's transport hub continues to create good jobs for Singaporeans?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Ultimately, that must remain our measure of success, not simply more passengers, more containers or more cargo, but better career, higher wages and meaningful opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Technology is already transforming aviation, maritime and logistics.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Second, Mr Deputy Speaker, much has been said about aviation and maritime.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: When people hear the word "logistics", they often think about the action of moving goods from one place to another.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: But increasingly, that is not where value is created.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The real value lies in planning, data, visibility and supply chain resilience, in the ability to anticipate disruptions before they happen and increasingly, in AI.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Singapore has always moved up the value chain.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: We did not remain simply a trading post.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Likewise, we should not remain simply a place where goods pass through.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: We should aspire to become the nerve centre of regional supply chains, where transport networks are planned, where supply chains are coordinated and where decisions are made.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: We should be the region’s "supply chain control tower".

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: We already have many of the building blocks: a world-class airport, a world-class port, trusted institution and strong digital infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The jobs of tomorrow will increasingly be in transport analytics, digital trade, AI-enabled planning, supply chain optimisation and sustainability.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: These are professional, managerial and specialist roles that will create greater value and better careers for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: T5 is one of the most significant infrastructure investments in our nation's history.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: It will strengthen Singapore's aviation hub for decades to come.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: But perhaps we should be thinking beyond T5 itself.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Together with the Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal, Changi Airfreight Centre, Changi Business Park, Loyang Industrial Park and our close proximity to the BBK Free Trade Zone, eastern Singapore has the potential to become an integrated gateway for aviation, maritime connectivity, logistics, business and tourism.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Rather than viewing them as separate developments, could we bring them together under one long-term vision?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Could stronger integration between T5 and the Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal create a seamless air-sea connection, making Singapore the preferred gateway for travellers and businesses connecting through the Indonesia-Malaysia-Singapore growth region?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Could this also catalyse new investments, create new businesses and generate even more good jobs for Singaporeans?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: I would gladly lobby for this vision with Sharael, especially since much of the infrastructure sits within Changi.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Another generation built one of the world's finest airports.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Our generation must now build the next chapter – not simply by expanding our infrastructure, but by creating more value through technology, innovation and our people.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: When my residents ask me whether Singapore will continue to create good jobs as our transport hub evolves, I believe our answer must be a resounding yes.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: That means continuing to invest boldly, embracing new technologies, moving up the value chain and ensuring that Singaporeans remain at the heart of our transport story.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: But honestly, Mr Deputy Speaker, truth be told, besides good jobs, my residents will also greatly appreciate an enhanced bus connectivity to Changi Airport and the Cargo Centre.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: But I will save that for another debate.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Ports can be built, airports can be expanded, but a future-ready workforce cannot simply be assembled overnight.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: If Singapore is to remain a leading global transport hub over the next two or three decades, our human capital strategy has to evolve with our infrastructure strategy.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Digitalisation, AI and automation are reshaping aviation, maritime and logistics.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: The jobs of tomorrow will certainly demand different skillsets, stronger interdisciplinary capabilities and a commitment to lifelong learning.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: The key challenge then is to ensure that our education system and our training pathways evolve just as quickly or even quicker, to keep up with the pace.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: The question is this, do our IHLs provide sufficient opportunities for students of today to combine engineering with AI, logistics with data analytics or maritime operations with digital technologies?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Equally important, are we providing enough opportunities for today's workers to continuously reskill as technology evolves?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Our transport strategy should therefore not simply be viewed as purely an infrastructure strategy.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: It should also keep in mind that it has to be a human capital strategy as well.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Singapore has always stayed ahead because we invested in our people ahead of demand.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Doing so would also reinforce one of the key objectives of this Motion, which is to anchor good jobs in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: If we do that well, technology will strengthen our workforce rather than displace it.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Singapore's transport success has never depended solely on just our ports, runways or logistics networks.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: It has always depended on our quality, adaptability and resilience of our workers and our people.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I believe we can better develop Singaporeans who will become the future leaders of the transport sector, identify where the skills gaps lie and determine how our existing platforms can better support this transition.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: We should plan our people with that same discipline and rigour.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: If we do so, I am confident that Singapore will continue to be not just a global transport hub, but a global transport leader.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I also thank Members of this Chamber who have spoken so far, for their wide range of ideas that have been expressed.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: While I may not be able to respond to every idea individually, MOT will take all of these suggestions back and consider them seriously.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Typically, when I am at this podium, I am speaking about local transport issues.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And no doubt, I will continue to do that.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Such is the life of the Transport Minister.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We recognise that transport touches the lives of every Singaporean – whether one drives, walks, cycles or rides.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But today, Ms Tin and our colleagues are asking us a different question: to consider the economic impact of transport, which cuts to the heart of how our country makes its living in a changed world.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But the worth of this sector goes far beyond GDP and jobs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Transport is the foundation on which our economy is built.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Where others might have seen a sleepy fishing village, the British looked at our deep harbour and saw a gateway to seaborne trade.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Today, our world-class airport and seaport connect Singapore to every major market on the planet.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Through them flows trade, many times the size of our own economy.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And this foundation is how Singapore was able to build everything else – an advanced manufacturing base, a high-value services hub and a young but growing engine for startups and enterprises.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: At this year's Committee of Supply, I set out three directions for our transport sector: to be globally-oriented, future-focused and people-centric.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This remains our north star and it is how I will frame my response to the Motion.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I will focus on MOT's overall strategies and Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling and Minister of State Baey Yam Keng will share more details on specific initiatives afterwards.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As more than a few Members have already observed, competing in today's world has become far more challenging.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Just this year, the Strait of Hormuz was closed for almost four months, upending global energy and supply chains.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And the disruption is not yet fully behind us.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: There were even suggestions from others that countries could levy tolls for passage – as though the right of transit passage guaranteed under UNCLOS simply did not exist.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We depend on a rules-based international order – one where every nation, large or small, operates on the same terms.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And this is why Singapore spoke up on Hormuz.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Because if the rules can be broken there, we worry they can be broken in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore too.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And what is done on the seas, could also be done in the skies above us.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For a country that lives by its connections, these rules are a matter of survival.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In November last year, I was in London for the Assembly of the IMO.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Meeting after meeting, one topic was raised – the IMO Net-Zero Framework.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: What troubled people was not so much the outcome that the vote would be delayed for a year.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It was a deeper question: does might make right?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: If a few powerful countries could arm-twist others and override a deal that was thought to be settled, then what does this mean for the future of the rules-based international order?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: What does this mean for countries that depend on this to prosper?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: One might draw from this a bleak conclusion that international organisations like the IMO have lost their relevance.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: When institutions come under strain, that is precisely the moment that a country like ours must show up – to bridge divides and to forge consensus on what matters.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Singapore speaks our mind, not only on our own interests, but on what we believe to be right for the world.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In the Council elections for the IMO and for the ICAO last year, Singapore received the highest number of votes in our category.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We may be a small country, but we are not a spectator.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, I agree with Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Sharael Taha that we must continue to strengthen Singapore's role as a global thought leader in transport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Singapore must do our part to shape global rules and standards so that they continue to work for small countries like ours.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Our presence in international organisations is only one part of our global orientation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This is why our transport companies like PSA, CAG, SATS and SIA are able to grow overseas and operate global networks.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We will deepen these links and build new ones with like-minded partners – bilaterally and multilaterally.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This includes new initiatives with our ASEAN neighbours: to make cross-border travel more seamless; to improve the efficiency and sustainability of regional ports; and to enhance regional air navigation and liberalise air services within and beyond ASEAN.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Next year, when Singapore takes on the ASEAN Chairmanship, we will have the opportunity to advance these projects and more, to bring our region closer together.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Is our current approach for global connectivity enough for this new world?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The Economic Strategy Review recently released its recommendations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: You may expect the Transport Minister to say that the answer is to build bigger and better airports and seaports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: That is still part of the plan, in case I inadvertently give my colleagues at the Ministry of Finance the wrong impression.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But several Members have noted that connectivity today no longer rests on physical infrastructure alone, and I agree.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Supply chains are becoming more fragmented and more distributed.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: If Singapore is merely a place through which flows happen to pass, then one day those flows will simply pass us by.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And that is why our strategy is not to rely on physical connectivity alone.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It is to build a host ecosystem that the industry is reliant on.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Ms Poh Li San already explained eloquently how the ecosystem approach works around our airport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Around our port, we have built a maritime industry ecosystem – ship financing, marine insurance, maritime law, arbitration.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Ms Gho Sze Kee, as an industry insider, vividly described this earlier in her speech much better than I could.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: All this is integrated with our supply chain and logistics ecosystem, which includes air freight forwarding as well as inland transport and logistics.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It has taken us decades of effort to build this ecosystem.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It is a strategic advantage that keeps Singapore, Tuas Port and PSA competitive and relevant, even as the physical flows of trade shift around us.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Mr Gerald Giam and Mr Kenneth Tiong spoke about Maersk.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Coincidentally, the chief executive officer of Maersk, Mr Vincent Clerc, called on the Prime Minister and me just two weeks ago.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Maersk is the second largest shipping line in the world by container volume.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It recognises the value of our broader maritime and logistics ecosystem.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It may have moved its transshipment operations to Tanjung Pelepas in the year 2000, but its Asia headquarters remain in Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In fact, Maersk manages its entire Asia and Middle East portfolio of port terminals, including Tanjung Pelepas, from Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, even when its cargo does not physically pass through our waters, the decisions about that cargo may still be made here and we are able to capture value from it.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As supply chains become more digital, connectivity will increasingly depend on technology.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This brings me to the second part of our strategy, which is to be future-focused.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Members have spoken a great deal about frontier technology, including AI.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Colleagues are correct to dwell on this topic.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: AI will profoundly reshape our economy and our society in ways that we cannot yet fully understand or imagine.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Like the Internet, we can be certain that AI will change our lives, long before we can say exactly how.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Thirty years ago, when web browsers started coming into public use, few of us would be prescient enough to have imagined that banking, shopping and even ride-hailing would one day all run through the Internet.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In the same way, we cannot predict precisely the shape of how AI will change our lives.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But we must prepare for it now, to stay ahead.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In the age of AI, it is even more important to have clarity on what makes Singapore successful in the first place.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Shippers and travellers choose Singapore not because we have the best proprietary technologies, but because we are more efficient, we are more connected and we are more reliable than the alternatives.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Technology is only one ingredient in our secret sauce.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Our approach will not be to adopt AI for its own sake, but to do so with intention, with clarity and on our own terms.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The National AI Council, chaired by the Prime Minister, drives our efforts on AI.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We begin with a real problem drawn from the industry and we ask what AI can do about it.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This approach suits the transport sector especially well, because our companies like PSA, SIA and SATS are already at the frontier, and we have a real opportunity to grow them into global champions in their own fields.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I am grateful to the Transport GPC Members who crafted this Motion for their thoughtful reference to frontier technologies.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Ms Tin, in particular, suggested that we beef up R&D to benefit Singapore's growth.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And this will include projects drawn from the AI Connectivity Mission.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We will use these funds to back ideas that could completely transform how transport operates today.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Ms Tin will be pleased to know that the MOT team does intend to explore how we can expand this into an intermodal concept across our air, land and sea networks.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: That brings me to the third part of our strategy, which is that transport must be people-centric.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Many Members have emphasised that technology is not about machines but about people, and I fully agree.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: On the economic front, it is about supporting our workers – making their jobs easier, more productive and more skilled.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: There will be many more jobs than workers available, but we will not be able to meet this growth by hiring 50% more.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: During Ramadan this year, I broke fast with some workers at Changi Airport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: One was a team of air traffic controllers.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: They shared with me how demanding their jobs are – watching several screens at once, deciding in real time what to tell each aircraft, making certain that no instruction conflicts with another, including with counterparts in neighbouring countries.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It is a job of extraordinary demand and a job with no margin for error.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: SATS workers are the backbone of our airport operations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: They are the reason why your baggage comes out so soon after you land.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: When we are at the airport, we walk on soft carpets, we enjoy air-conditioning, we listen to calming ambient music.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But behind the scenes, there is an army of SATS workers doing backbreaking work, amid the heat and the noise, to move your baggage from the tarmac to the belt.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: These are exactly the types of work that AI can lighten.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For the air traffic controller, AI can put the full picture together so that the controller is free to do only what a human can: weigh the options, make a decision and carry the final call.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For the SATS worker, AI can automate physical and repetitive processes so that he or she is in a safer and more comfortable environment while taking on responsibilities that make better use of their skills.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Technology of this kind raises the value of the worker.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: As Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Sanjeev Tiwari, among others, put it, workers can enjoy better wages, better welfare and better work prospects.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Technology can transform existing jobs and also create new jobs that did not exist before.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I am glad Mr Ang Wei Neng spoke extensively about the new opportunities that AVs will bring.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: These opportunities are precisely why my Ministry has been preparing for AVs at the airport, at the seaport and also on our roads.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Recently, I gave out scholarships to children of ComfortDelGro's driver-partners.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I met many proud parents, most of whom have been drivers for more than 10 years.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We chatted about what their children were planning to study – engineering, computer science, finance.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: All of the parents had one thing in common: they wanted their children to do better in life than they did.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I shared with them the new exciting jobs that AVs will bring – software developers, robotics designers, vehicle engineers and so on.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Jobs that many of their sons and daughters would love to take on.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I explained that the Government is preparing for AVs for the same reason that we invest in our children's education – we are giving them a better future.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I know there is concern amongst our taxi and private-hire car drivers about AVs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling and I meet the driver unions very regularly.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
