text: Driver jobs are not going to vanish anytime soon.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In contrast, we only have about 20 AVs running around our roads, mostly in Punggol.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, AVs are not displacing today's drivers, and even in 10 years, I expect that we will still require many human drivers.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Our plan is indeed to take a proactive approach to support our drivers in any transition.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Technology matters and we will keep investing in it.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But the future of transport is not about robotaxis or about drones or the smartest AI brain.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Last month, I was in Chongqing in China.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Her name was Jocelyn, a young and energetic woman.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: She was on her first overseas posting – the only SIA staff in that office.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: There is one flight to and from Singapore daily, but it is at a godforsaken hour, landing at 1.15 am and departing at 2.35 am.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, Jocelyn is out at the airport in the middle of the night and gets home to sleep only at 4.00 am.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But from my conversations with her, I could tell that she loves her job – living in a new city, working in a new culture, learning about herself as she strives in a new environment.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We can offer young Singaporeans like Jocelyn such opportunities because of the global reach of our transport sector.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Because we build firmly with an eye on the future.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: That is what all of us at MOT are striving for.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Not technology for its own sake, not staying number one for its own sake, but so that our children, and theirs after them, can reach for opportunities that we ourselves never had.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We hold the line on the rules so that a small nation is never left at the mercy of a large one.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We invest at the frontier so that our hard-won lead is not quietly surrendered.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We do all of it for one reason and one reason only – for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For the Singaporeans of today and for the Singaporeans of tomorrow who will one day do things that we in this Chamber have not yet even imagined.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The transition towards electrified mobility is one of the defining shifts in transport today.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It is driven by climate imperatives, rapid technological progress, improving vehicle economics and the need for greater energy efficiency.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Electric vehicles (EVs) use energy more efficiently than internal combustion engines and their wider adoption can help Singapore reduce emissions, improve local air quality and build a more sustainable transport system.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The Government's approach has been comprehensive – reducing upfront ownership costs, building charging infrastructure ahead of demand, introducing appropriate standards and regulations, and progressively transitioning public transport and commercial fleets.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: As of March 2026, around 30,500 charging points had already been deployed, indicating that progress is being made at scale.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The growing take-up of EVs demonstrates that the policy framework is beginning to work.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Consumers now have a broader selection of EV models across price points, while the rapid expansion of charging infrastructure is reducing range anxiety, making EV ownership more practical for households.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: However, the transition will not be uniform across all vehicle segments.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: For private cars and light commercial vehicles, the economics are improving quickly.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In 2014, EVs accounted for about one-third of new car registrations, while roughly half of the new light goods vehicle registrations were electric.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The more difficult challenge lies in heavy vehicles.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Heavy goods vehicles, construction vehicles, coaches, waste-management fleets and other commercial vehicles operate differently from private cars.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: They travel longer distances, carry heavier loads, face tighter operating schedules and often require reliable charging at depots rather than at public carparks.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: This is why the Government's recent heavy-vehicle measures are important.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: These chargers must be deployed at designated lorry or coach lots, or at the vehicle owner's place of business.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: These are sensible interventions because the barrier to heavy-vehicle electrification is not simply the vehicle purchase price.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It is the entire operating ecosystem: depot space, electrical capacity, charging downtime, route scheduling, fleet financing and residual-value risk.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: For smaller commercial vehicles, the transition is already more advanced.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The Commercial Vehicle Emissions Scheme support electric light commercial vehicles, while higher-emission diesel vehicles face increasing surcharges.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Public buses provide the clearest example of how fleet electrification can scale when vehicle procurement, charging infrastructure and operational planning are coordinated.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Singapore is working towards a cleaner-energy public bus fleet by 2040, with electric buses expected to make up around half of the fleet by 2030.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The near-term opportunity is therefore clear, and the medium-term test is whether Singapore can create the conditions for broader adoption among logistics operators, construction firms, waste-management companies and other heavy-duty fleet owners.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: First, we should ensure that fleet operators, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, can access attractive financing and leasing options for electric commercial vehicles.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Second, we should continue to facilitate charging infrastructure at industrial estates, logistics facilities, depots and designated heavy-vehicle parking areas.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The availability of electricity connections, charging equipment and operational space will be just as important as the vehicle purchase incentive itself.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Agencies such as LTA, JTC and the Energy Market Authority and the private sector should continue to work closely to identify priority locations where commercial fleet charging demand is likely to emerge first.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Third, we should leverage digital technologies to improve fleet utilisation.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Smart charging systems, route optimisation, predictive maintenance and energy-management software can help fleet operators reduce downtime and manage electricity costs more effectively.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: This is where electrification and digitalisation come together.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It is a pity that the Singapore-Kuala Lumpur High Speed Rail (HSR) did not go ahead in January 2021, after many years of feasibility studies, planning and negotiations.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Both Singapore and Malaysia announced the joint development of the HSR in February 2013 and subsequently signed a legally binding Bilateral Agreement in December 2016, establishing the governance framework for what would have been Southeast Asia's most transformative infrastructure projects.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The HSR would have provided a compelling new mode of travel between Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, reducing journey times from more than four hours by road to approximately 90 minutes, with trains operating at speeds of up to 320 kilometres per hour.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Had the project proceeded as originally planned, services would have commenced by the end of this year.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And that is why HSR at this range in other places has captured massive market share in outperforming air travel in terms of total door-to-door travel time.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The strategic merits of the project remain compelling.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: First, it would deepen economic integration between Singapore and Malaysia by strengthening connectivity between Southeast Asia's two leading business centres, facilitating business travel and encouraging greater cross-border trade and investment.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Second, it would promote more balanced regional development.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Intermediate cities such as Melaka, Muar and Batu Pahat stood to benefit from increased investment, tourism and business activity arising from improved accessibility.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Similarly for Singapore, the project would also have catalysed urban redevelopment.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: For example, the planned terminus at Jurong East was envisaged as a key anchor for the development of the Jurong Lake District as our second Central Business District.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Third, the HSR would encourage a shift away from road and air travel.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: A reliable 90-minute rail journey would offer an attractive alternative to short-haul flights, easing congestion at airports or on highways while supporting both countries' sustainability objectives.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Nevertheless, the long-term strategic case for the HSR remains strong.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Beyond transport connectivity, it has the potential to strengthen regional competitiveness, enhance economic resilience and support long-term urban and economic development on both sides of the Causeway.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I therefore encourage the Government to continue engaging its Malaysian counterpart on this issue, including through the Leaders' Retreat and other bilateral platforms.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Even if the implementation is not imminent, it is worthwhile to keep the dialogue active, keep exploring innovative financing and operating models, and remain prepared should the opportunity arise to realise a project that delivers mutual benefits for both Singapore and Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Realising this potential may require us to rethink legacy arrangements, redesign established operating models and embed new technologies more deeply across the economy.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Done well, these changes can improve economic competitiveness, strengthen sustainability and enhance our resilience in an increasingly uncertain world.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: It is the result of decades of investment, sound policy and above all, generations of transport workers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Because of my work as the Executive Secretary of the National Transport Workers' Union (NTWU) and Advisor to the National Taxi Association (NTA), the National Private Hire Vehicles Association (NPHVA), I wish to take this opportunity to speak up for our transport workers as we advance Singapore's position as a global transport hub.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: As we discuss Singapore's future, let us also remember the people who make that future possible every single day – the bus captains, rail workers, taxi and private hire drivers, logistics workers, technicians, aircrew, seafarers who keep Singapore moving, often long before dawn and long after midnight.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They are not simply part of our transport system, they are the reason it works.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: AI, robotics and frontier technologies will undoubtedly transform transport.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Used wisely, technology can make work safer, more productive and more meaningful.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: But if transitions are poorly managed, they can also create uncertainty and definitely anxiety.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: As we embrace an AI-enabled transport system, especially one of global significance, we must re-imagine, with workers at the heart of the process, what jobs, skills and careers will look like in this future.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Because when we truly listen to workers, we will stop asking: "Which jobs will disappear?", "How many jobs will be displaced?" Instead, we begin asking better questions: "What strengths do our workers already possess so that we can build the future around those strengths?", "What practical barriers must we remove if we want workers to embrace transformation?", "And what support must we provide so that no worker is left behind?" Over the last few months, together with my union leaders and NTUC colleagues, I have spent considerable time on the ground through focus group discussions and individual engagements with bus captains, taxi drivers and private hire drivers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Every day, our transport workers witness our transport system transforming right before their eyes.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They know AI and new technologies are changing the way we move.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They are understandably anxious, but they are also curious.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Following the Economic Strategy Review, our workers understand that Singapore must continue to innovate and remain competitive.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They are not asking us to slow down.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They are asking not to be left behind.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Eve has been driving a taxi for the past 12 years.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: She put it more eloquently than I could ever.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: We must ensure that everyone move forward together with technology. : Technology should move Singapore forward.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: But the true measure of progress is whether it brings our people forward with it.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Our transport workers are asking a deeply human question: "Where do I fit in the future of Singapore as a global transport hub?" Our workers want to know what opportunities technology might create, what skills they should begin building today and how they can continue contributing meaningfully tomorrow.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Our workers ask for a fair and thoughtful transition, they want the assurance that they will not be left to navigate this change alone because the clarity they seek is not simply about jobs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: It is about lives; it is about livelihoods.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: For Mr Low, a taxi driver in his early 40s, it means having the flexibility to earn a living while caring for his 64-year-old mother and taking her for her medical appointments.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: For Aly, who drives a combi-limo, it means earning enough to provide a better future for her five young daughters.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: For Ah Ban, who proudly became Singapore's first EV taxi driver, it means continuing to build a career that he takes pride in as the industry evolves.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: And for Harry, after 31 years behind the wheel, retirement does not mean stepping away from transport.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: He imagines a future where owning an AV fleet with his friends becomes the next chapter of his working life – a retirement built not on stopping work, but on the experience he has spent three decades building.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: These are stories of real drivers and those are their real names.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: But this is what our workers are asking for.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Not certainty about the future – none of us can promise that, but clarity that there is a place for them in it.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: As we continue building Singapore as a global business and transport hub, we must do more than create the industries of tomorrow.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: We must also redesign the jobs of tomorrow, making work safer, more productive and more meaningful, while keeping our workers' needs and livelihoods at the heart of every of these transformations.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: We have already seen how this can work in real life.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: In doing so, SBS Transit developed new specialist capabilities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: In this case, technology did not replace our workers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Through our engagements, we also heard about the practical barriers our transport workers face as they prepare for transition.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Every hour spent in training is an hour of forgone income.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: For many, attending a course is not simply about setting aside time.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: It also means paying vehicle rental, covering operating costs and giving up precious earning opportunities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: The opportunity cost of transformation is therefore much higher for our P2P drivers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: If transformation is at too high a personal cost, even the best training programme will struggle to succeed.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Our drivers are also deeply pragmatic about upskilling.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They understand that they must continue learning to remain relevant, whether within or beyond the transport industry.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: But they have also told us, time and time again, that training must lead somewhere.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: It must open the door to real jobs, real opportunities and of course, sustainable livelihoods.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: After all, our drivers have mortgages to pay, ageing parents to care for and children to raise.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: It is one of the profession's defining features.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Many drivers chose this career precisely because it allows them to balance caregiving responsibilities, family commitments and other life circumstances.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: If we want them to embrace lifelong learning, then our training ecosystem must be equally flexible.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Allow me to suggest three areas for action.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: First, transformation works best when workers help to design it.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Job redesign must begin before disruption occurs, and workers and unions must be part of the conversation right from the outset.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: We cannot design the future of work without workers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Second, workers need visible and credible pathways into future jobs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: For bus captains, future roles should continue building on valuable capabilities that they have already developed – managing commuters, responding to real-world situations and ensuring passenger safety.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: For our taxi and private-hire drivers, emerging opportunities such as safety operators and remote operators should provide meaningful pathways into the AV ecosystem.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Their years of road experience will strengthen the safety and operational readiness of future mobility services.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: The transition support we provide matters too, particularly for workers whose livelihoods depend on being behind the wheel every day.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: We should create more flexible training pathways, Place and Train programmes, strengthen company-level apprenticeships and expand flexible work arrangements to include flexible training arrangements.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: For technicians and skilled tradesmen, the shift towards electrification presents one of the greatest opportunities for workforce transformation.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Singapore must position itself not only as a leader in electric mobility, but also as a regional centre of excellence for EV maintenance, battery systems and digital diagnostics.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Roles such as EV technicians and EV technical specialists will become increasingly valuable as transport systems across the world become more technologically sophisticated.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Around the world, countries are already investing heavily in these specialised capabilities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They must see how our workers can progress from technician, to specialist, to diagnostic expert and eventually into engineering, supervisory and leadership positions.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: When workers can clearly see both the skills required and the pathway ahead, they are far more likely to embrace change with confidence.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: As we transform the transport sector, let us also measure whether transformation is delivering what truly matters – not simply more technology, but better jobs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Third, AVs must complement our drivers, not compete against them.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: The tripartite has already begun important work through various workgroups and steering committees to guide Singapore's national AV deployment.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: This is a nascent space and it is important that the Labour Movement continues to have a seat at the table.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: We will continue speaking up for workers on deployment concerns, liability and regulatory frameworks, and more importantly, how the AV industry can create good local jobs and build Singaporean capabilities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: We look forward to seeing workers' views incorporated into MOT's national AV deployment plans.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: I am glad this sentiment was also raised earlier by the hon Member Ang Wei Neng and his constituents.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: As a tripartite, we can and we must ensure that AVs become another opportunity to strengthen rather than weaken our workers' prospects and livelihoods.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: (In Mandarin):   Our taxi drivers, private-hire drivers and bus captains are not afraid of new technology.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: They simply want to know that when AVs arrive, will there be a place for them?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Technological progress should make the work of drivers safer and more dignified, not cost them their livelihoods.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: That answer is not simply another training course.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I rise on this Motion as a Member of this House and also as the Chair of the GPC for Defence and Foreign Affairs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I mention the second because for us, transport policy is inseparable from foreign policy and national security.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To talk about our ports and airports is to talk about our place in this world.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some 700 years ago, the trading cities of the Hanseatic League built the most successful commercial network in Europe – not because their ports were the biggest, but because merchants knew what to expect.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The harbour cities of Srivijaya and Melaka understood the same truth.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The most valuable port is not the largest.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is why we still exist as a trading nation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But world-class infrastructure alone, however necessary, has never been sufficient.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Supply chains today are shaped by geopolitics as much as by cost.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For Singapore, decisions about transport are decisions about our economy, our diplomacy and our security.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A new berth is worth only what the world thinks of the country behind it.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our task is not just to build, but to shape the environment around what we build so the jobs stay here.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have three proposals: one about our region, one about ourselves and one about the wider world.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Each of them aimed at what this Motion affirms: long-term competitiveness through cooperation with our neighbours, the technologies of the frontier and the infrastructure the world can rely on so that good jobs stay anchored here.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For centuries, Johor, Singapore and the Riau Islands worked as one trading system along the Straits of Malacca through which a third of world trade still flows.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone gives all three a chance to knit that older geography back together, not politically, but economically.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our job is to make sure the ecosystem grows with it, on both sides of the Causeway and beyond.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Aviation, shipping, logistics headquarters, customs, trade finance, maritime law, supply chain command.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These functions need trust and trust is what we have spent 60 years building.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My father worked at PSA for 40 years, directing containers on the ground, shift after shift, under the sun and in the rain.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: He was one of thousands of ordinary Singaporeans whose hands built the port that built modern Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Today, at Tuas, some of his successors sit in air-conditioned control rooms and run 20 cranes at once, guided by AI, in a port that is increasingly running itself.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Their work is safer, their pay is better, their skills are sharper.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But the reason they exist is the same reason he did.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Singapore has to be a place the world can rely on.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: That is what this Motion is really about.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is about honouring those who built this port with their hands and giving the next generation the tools to run it in a very different timeline.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I know the question this will provoke in this Chamber and across the Causeway.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is being asked in Johor and Riau too.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If we integrate more with our neighbours, will the good jobs not simply move?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But the jobs that we have always been trusted to do best will not move – financing, brokering, customs, maritime law, air traffic control, supply chain command.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And equally, the engineers, technicians, marine crews and training pathways from ITE and polytechnics to a control room.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We are not proposing to hand Singapore's value away.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We are proposing to grow Singapore, Johor and Riau together, each anchoring what it does best, connected by the trust the region has built.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: There is a proven model close to home.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Hong Kong International Airport's SkyPier ferries passengers from Shenzhen and other Pearl River Delta ports directly to airside.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They check in at their departure port, never clear Hong Kong immigration and arrive at their gate – something similar between Johor and Changi, jointly designed, we can build on together.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must negotiate it, earn it and build it patiently.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I would therefore ask the Government to look seriously at three practical measures.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, build cross-border transport into that system, coach, rail or ferry, integrated with our airlines from the moment a passenger sets off.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, establish digital customs clearance and bonded cargo corridors from southern Johor into PSA and the Changi Airfreight Centre.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Each of these measures is designed to benefit our neighbours as much as us.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A traveller checking in at Johor Bahru spends money there.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A cargo corridor creates jobs on both sides.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Batam and Bintan enter on the same terms.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our ambition should be for the wider region to become what it was for centuries: an integrated trading system in which each partner does what it does best and Singapore's role is to help hold it together.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A gateway means nothing if the country behind it is not reliable in a crisis.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Undersea cables in the Baltic have been cut again and again.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They are pressure on the arteries our economy depends on.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our position rests on trust: trust in freedom of navigation, trust in international law, trust that we will remain open and reliable whichever way the world turns.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Foreign interference is not just a security problem.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should not wait for a crisis to discover our weak points.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Preparation is a capability in its own right.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And when the next storm comes, the world has to know it can still count on us.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Preparation alone only manages a world we did not design.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If we want to help shape the century, not just weather it, we must do one more thing.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For 60 years, we have shown that we can compete under international rules.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The next 60 will require us to help write them.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Competition is no longer about products and prices.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is about who sets the standards, defines the technology, runs the institutions, and ultimately writes the rules.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Why should anyone follow rules written by a country of six million?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Because the rules a small country writes are not designed to favour a small country.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They must work for whoever sits at the table.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We can afford to write rules that treat every party fairly, because we cannot assume we will always be at the top.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: That is why our Digital Economy Agreements have been adopted by countries much larger than us.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is why the Housing Development Board (HDB), once heterodox, is now studied globally.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Singapore is credible as a contributor to those rules not because we insist on our own advantage, but because we do not.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Minister Chan Chun Sing made a related point at Shangri-La Dialogue last month.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: UNCLOS was written for a world in which oceans mainly carried ships.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Today, they carry the digital infrastructure of the world economy.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Over 99% of Singapore's international communications runs through undersea cables.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Countries that help set standards shape the markets that run on them and gain influence out of proportion to their size.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Through TradeTrust and our IMO work, we have done this before, by designing frameworks that are practical, neutral and useable everywhere.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Government, and not only MOT, should bring the same ambition into transport, logistics and the infrastructure that underpins them in four areas.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These are the four places where frontier technologies and international rules will meet.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Common standards for trusted digital trade and cargo certification, so Singapore-issued documents are honoured elsewhere without translation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Rules for autonomous shipping and AI in port operations, so questions of liability and accountability do not remain open as ships and ports run themselves.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Stronger international protection for undersea cables, for freedom of navigation through chokepoints, and for the infrastructure the digital economy sits on.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In the 20th century, we built the port.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In the 21st, we must help decide the rules the port will live under, not just how well we follow them.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our founders built a port where people could trust.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The next generation built an airport, a financial centre and a reputation the world came to rely on.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We will have to give solutions in a world that is increasingly difficult to navigate.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, build a national resilience that lets us stay reliable through a National Crisis Logistics Compact to stress test our supply chains, rehearse them, publish a Hub Resilience Statement and coordinate before crises arrive.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, move from a country that competes under international rules to one that helps write them.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And in the protection of undersea cables and chokepoint navigation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These may seem like transport proposals but are really national ones.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Connectivity has never just been an industry for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It has been our strategy and often our safety.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But we must also keep building our trust.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is the only infrastructure a small country cannot afford to lose.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Every generation since Independence has earned our place in the world.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our responsibility is to see that the next generation is given the chance to do the same.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They are reflected in the goods we received and the resilience we have when the world becomes more uncertain.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Members have spoken about what the future of transport could hold and why we must invest today to capture new opportunities tomorrow and remain competitive globally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The seeds of the future must be planted today, through sustained investments in technology, systems and our people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will elaborate on how our investments are strengthening our transport system today, while preparing Singapore for the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Transport connects Singapore to the world through our aviation and maritime networks, underpinning our competitiveness as a global hub.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We must continue to plan ahead and invest in the future of transport.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: First, how our investments are making a difference today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Second, why we must continue to innovate for the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: And third, why we must build the future together with the next generation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Across aviation, maritime and land transport, our investments are already improving reliability and efficiency today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Given the focus of this Motion, I will highlight examples from aviation and maritime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In aviation, CAAS invested in next-generation air traffic management concepts and tools, to optimise flight operations amidst growing traffic density.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: An example is the Regional Collaboration Platform, which is an experimentation tool that allows air navigation service providers to share information and optimise air traffic flows across the region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over time, this will lead to more punctual and predictable flights, as well as lower fuel use and emissions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MPA invested in smart port operations and vessel coordination, to improve efficiency across port activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, AI-enabled vessel voyage planning helps shipping companies plan more fuel-efficient routes and coordinate vessel arrivals more effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Although it is at the prototype stage, simulated trials have shown reduced fuel use, pointing to more efficient scheduling and faster turnaround times.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In a major hub like Singapore, this translates to lower costs and smoother, more reliable movement of goods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These examples show how our investments are strengthening reliability and efficiency of our transport system today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While we continue to improve the transport system today, we must also prepare for what lies ahead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: A key challenge is tightening manpower, even as our transport system becomes more complex.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As such, we are investing in autonomy to fundamentally improve how operations are carried out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will focus on new operating models involving AVs, vessels and robotics across our port, airport and logistics network.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This also builds on the point raised by Mr Ang Wei Neng on advancing the use of AVs in aviation and maritime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will allow us to handle higher volumes more efficiently and enable workers to focus on tasks that require human judgement and expertise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Once developed, we will pilot these solutions with the industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With our high volumes of cargo and supportive regulatory environment, Singapore can serve as a real-world "living lab" to test and deploy these solutions at scale.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Once proven here, they can be adopted internationally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This reinforces the point raised by Mr Jackson Lam, that Singapore should not only be a transport hub, but a transport innovation hub.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We must also improve how the transport system works as a whole.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Therefore, we will invest in digital twins to manage the transport network more intelligently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, by integrating data across port, airport and logistics network, we can track cargo flows in real-time, anticipate disruptions and adjust operations more effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This also aligns with Ms Tin Pei Ling's suggestion to deepen digital twin capabilities, alongside proposals by Mr Sharael Taha and Mr Edward Chia to move towards a more integrated sea-air logistics control tower.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To build our digital twins, we are strengthening our common digital infrastructure to facilitate sharing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are leveraging platforms such as SGTraDex, which Ms He Ting Ru had raised, to strengthen such sharing and seeking more partners for existing use cases and to drive new ones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: At the same time, we will continue to deepen sector-specific capabilities across aviation, maritime and land transport.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will elaborate on aviation and maritime which are closely related to this Motion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In aviation, we will focus on next-generation air navigation services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As air traffic grows, we need to manage more flights safely and efficiently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will invest in AI-enabled air traffic flow management to better balance traffic demand with airport capacity, enabling smoother and more efficient flights.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In maritime, we will continue to strengthen our smart maritime operations and services, and support the safe use of alternative maritime energy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As the sector transits to alternative fuels to reduce international shipping's carbon footprint, we will also invest in research to ensure they can be delivered and bunkered safely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Together, these efforts will help us to do more with less.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will make better use of our manpower in a tighter labour environment, while using less space and emitting less carbon so that Singapore remains strong as a global transport and connectivity hub.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Dennis Tan mentioned that Singapore cannot rely solely on adopting technologies developed elsewhere.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is why we are building our own capabilities in areas where we have unique strengths and operational advantages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ultimately, the value of innovation depends not just on what we develop, but how it is applied in real operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our SMEs will play an important role in making this happen.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As rightly pointed out by Mr Jackson Lam, Mr Edward Chia and Mr Lee Hong Chuang, SMEs are a critical part of our transport ecosystem and must be supported to digitalise and remain competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Government agencies have worked with the industry to support SMEs in adopting digital solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, the Sea Transport Industry Digital Plan provides a clear roadmap to guide maritime SMEs in adopting digital solutions at each stage of their growth while building the necessary skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To complement this, we have also introduced hands-on programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This helps them move from awareness to implementation, strengthening capabilities and improving productivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The next generation is critical to the future of transport.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They are not just future users of the system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They are our future planners, engineers, entrepreneurs and leaders who will shape what comes next.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have already seen how the next generation can make meaningful contributions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Tommy Phun and Ms Lyn Phun are carrying forward their family's maritime legacy from Eng Hup Shipping, which was founded in 1957.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Even earlier, their grandfather used to drive a wooden tongkang along the Singapore River.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Growing up, they spent much of their childhood in shipyards, immersed in the maritime environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These early experiences shaped their interest in the industry and they later chose to join it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They did more than just continue the business.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As the sector decarbonises, they founded Pyxis to develop electric vessels and introduce new technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Their journey shows how the next generation can build on what came before them and help transform the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is why we want to tap on this potential and build clear and structured pathways for the next generation, as highlighted by Dr Wan Rizal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The future of transport should be built for future generations and hence, it should be shaped with them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In Mandarin):   The future of transport is not only about technological advancement – it is also deeply tied to our national development and overall competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: What we are witnessing today is the fruit of labour, of generations before us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is precisely because of the strong foundation laid by our predecessors that we can keep innovating and introducing new technologies into this sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Encouragingly, a new generation is already injecting fresh energy into the industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Building on this legacy, they continue to innovate, propelling the industry towards a more efficient and sustainable future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This also means that the industry is opening up exciting new frontiers for growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our next generation will have far greater opportunities to make their mark here.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Government will also guide them into the transport sector through scholarships, training and career development pathways, so that they can put their talents to good use and contribute to society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The torch is passed from one generation to the next, and the flame burns on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The future of transport is being built for the next generation and so we must build it together with them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As long as we remain committed to technological innovation and the development of our people, Singapore's transport system will continue to improve and benefit all Singaporeans. : Mr Speaker, to conclude, our investments in transport research and innovation are strengthening our transport system today while preparing Singapore and Singaporeans for the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: By investing in both innovation and people, we aim to build a transport system that not only serves the future generations well, but one that they will help to shape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members have affirmed the strategic importance of transport and connectivity and shared their suggestions on how we can strengthen Singapore's long-term economic competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If we harness technology early and well to create opportunities and improve lives for our residents and our workers, we can thrive in an increasingly uncertain world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Several Members have highlighted that transformation must create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The use of technology helps us solve problems, but people will always remain at the heart of transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Experience, judgement, professionalism and care are not replaceable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our transport workforce will always be at the core of our transport services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Mr Sanjeev Kumar and Mr Wan Rizal have highlighted, we will work closely with tripartite partners to ensure that Singaporeans are well-positioned to seize these new opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: CAAS and NTUC have also announced a partnership to co-design an AI training roadmap for aviation union leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Autonomy and AI are at work across our Transport sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In Tuas port, automation has been built in from the ground up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Automated guided vehicles move containers and cranes are operated remotely, making it one of the most advanced container terminals in the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Trials for autonomous prime movers are also underway in Pasir Panjang terminal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I spoke to Mr Faiz who works at PSA in Pasir Panjang.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He used to drive a prime mover but has now transited to work in the control room as a remote operator for autonomous prime movers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He said that the workplace is now more comfortable and he is happier with the shift arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are investing in our maritime workforce just as deliberately across different stages of their career.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Together with our unions and partners, we have also enhanced the Tripartite Maritime Training Award for individuals seeking a seafaring career.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: New pathways into shore-based roles are opening, such as Singapore Management University's Industry Graduate Diploma in Maritime for mid-career transitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Additionally, as Mr Dennis Tan mentioned, we want to prepare Singaporeans to take on leadership roles in the maritime sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As maritime is global in nature, maritime leaders will need to have experience and capabilities running international operations and managing cross-cultural teams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And this is why we have launched a new Maritime Cluster Fund Global Rotation Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The scheme provides grants to companies to co-fund the overseas deployments of local middle-managers to equip them with the competencies to take on supervisory roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On our roads, the deployment of AVs can help us meet our connectivity needs, ease manpower constraints in public transport and improve safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Grab and ComfortDelGro currently operate 16 fixed route autonomous shuttles in Punggol.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Safety operators are on board to ensure safety in this initial deployment phase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As of June this year, close to 10,000 unique riders have taken the shuttles and 99% of them surveyed said they felt safe and they would recommend the ride to others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Riders provided feedback that they would like more destinations, direct connections and flexible bookings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will work with the operators to improve the service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree with Mr Ang Wei Neng's suggestion that AVs should first be deployed to serve underserved areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will progressively extend AVs to new areas with clear transport needs and are considering areas, such as Sentosa, Tuas and Mandai as possibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, in response to Mr Ang Wei Neng's and Mr Fadli Fawzi's points, further deployment must be realistic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The technology for AV buses is not as mature compared to that of AV cars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Current autonomous bus models also have a smaller passenger capacity compared to our public buses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Public buses also have to meet the needs of different commuters – such as the elderly, parents with children in strollers and persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Hence, the operational aspects of autonomous public buses have to be worked through to meet the needs of different commuters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That said, we agree that there are good use cases for autonomous buses, such as night bus services, and we will consider it when the technology is more mature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As autonomy grows across our airport, seaport and roads, new job opportunities will emerge in areas such as fleet management and remote operations, autonomous EV engineering as well as business development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We recognise that autonomy and AI, if not managed well, can bring disruption to existing jobs, industries and business models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The ultimate purpose of using technology is to benefit people – our residents and our workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Technology's worth lies in the problems it solves and the lives it improves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will roll out the use of autonomy and AI at a pace acceptable to residents, commuters and drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As the Acting Minister has mentioned, the introduction of AVs will be a gradual process to give our commuters and drivers time to adapt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have been engaging taxi and private hire drivers early as we want to ensure that our drivers are well-equipped to seize job opportunities from this transition and that they can stay ahead of this change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I recently met leaders from the NTA and NPHVA again, together with Ms Yeo Wan Ling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The union leaders ask what they can do to equip themselves and their members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is for drivers looking to transition into new roles that come with up to 90% salary support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will introduce a CCP for drivers keen to pivot to the AVs sector, known as the "CCP for Autonomous Vehicle specialists".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Like all CCPs, participants will be offered employment prior to the commencement of the programme and training supported by the SWDA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: GrabAcademy, Grab's training arm, has been onboarded as a registered training provider with SWDA to deliver AV-related training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For drivers who wish to pivot to other transport related jobs such as Bus captains, we will introduce a new pathway under the "CCP for Public Transport Professionals".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This follows recent announcements we have made regarding increasing salaries and sign on bonuses for new bus captains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Drivers who are keen to move into other sectors can tap on existing programmes offered by the SWDA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, we will pilot a new training incentive scheme from January 2027, focusing on short-form courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Drivers do not just forego some income when they go for training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This training incentive amount is significantly higher than any other training allowances currently offered as we understand that drivers have additional expenditure like car rentals to manage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Drivers can tap on this incentive to acquire new skills before committing to longer-term programmes, such as the CCPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, we will launch a new one-stop webpage with relevant information and resources curated for drivers and to raise awareness of the new support measures available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some of our drivers are already taking steps to thrive in this future of mobility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Ang Li Wei used to drive a taxi with ComfortDelGro, but she seized the opportunity to train as a safety operator for AVs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: She believes AVs will change the scene of driving worldwide, and she also sees new and more specialised roles emerging for drivers, such as helping wheelchair users, families with young children and others who need extra care on their journeys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Tong is actually here with us today in the Gallery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Tong has spent over a decade behind the wheel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He qualified as a safety operator and he has gone on to get certification as a remote operator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In his words, he wants a front-row seat as to where the industry is heading.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Tong says he wants to support our efforts towards the future of mobility, about the future of AVs, so he is here with us today, despite his very busy schedule.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government will take a proactive approach to help workers adapt, support job transitions and to equip Singaporeans with the skills and capabilities needed in the age of autonomy and AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The manpower transition package is one of more upcoming moves we are putting in place for our P2P drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to work closely with the unions and support our workers as jobs evolve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The advancement of technology and the application of AI have given rise to cause for concern.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, whether people's livelihoods might be affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our taxi and private-hire drivers are no exception.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some of you have worked with taxi companies for many years; some found flexible work with Grab after a career transition; some are very familiar with the streets of Singapore and have excellent driving skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Regardless of your background, you share one thing in common: you work hard every day to earn a living for your families and shoulder your responsibilities at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Each day, you race against time to make it easier and more convenient for Singaporeans to get around.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the face of innovations such as AI and AVs, I believe we must always keep the interests of our transport workers in mind and be people-centric.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I have always believed that the ultimate purpose of technology is to benefit people – residents and workers alike.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Based on the current situation, AVs will introduced gradually and progressively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOT will roll out new technologies and AI at a pace that residents, passengers and drivers are comfortable with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We hope this will help our drivers seize the employment opportunities that this technological transformation brings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I believe that technology is not an end in itself.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The well-being of Singaporeans is the objective behind all our efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As we work to enhance Singapore's transport efficiency and technological edge, we remain committed to protecting the livelihoods and well-being of our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I am confident that as long as the Government, businesses, and workers strive together towards this common goal, we will not only be able to navigate this new wave of technological change, but also seize the opportunities that it brings to build a better future together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, in English please.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our air hub is one of Singapore's crown jewels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Changi Airport's story is one of deliberate ambition, constant reinvention and an unwavering commitment to connect us to the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To address Mr Edward Chia's, Mr Sharael Taha's and Ms Valerie Lee's suggestion on strengthening Changi's connectivity to other parts of Singapore and the region, we are studying how to best enable seamless air-sea transfers between Changi Airport and Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal, and synergise future developments in the wider Changi region including Changi Business Park, Changi Village and Loyang.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree with Mr Fadli Fawzi's suggestion, that infrastructure should also improve Singaporeans' lived experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Changi East Urban district will be a new lifestyle and business hub for Singaporeans and visitors to connect, work and play.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Expanding Changi Airport gives us an opportunity to rethink existing processes, increase productivity and transform jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Poh Li San has rightly highlighted that many roles in ground-handling and facilities management are physically demanding and will increasingly take its toll on our ageing workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree with Mr Gerald Giam's point that digital tools should benefit workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Changi Airport has been deploying automation, robotics and AI to improve the safety and productivity of our workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since January 2026, autonomous baggage tractors are used to move passenger bags between terminals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They spare workers from repetitive driving, reduces fatigue and frees them up for complex and safety-critical last mile services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: From driving a single tractor, a worker can now oversee and coordinate a fleet of vehicles or be trained to maintain the vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The new job role is more sustainable and offers a higher pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In time, autonomous tractors can be used to move cargo and airside equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Technology tools can also be used to optimise work planning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: OpsAssist is an AI Tool that SATS uses to enable better manpower and equipment allocation for each aircraft turnaround.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: OpsAssist also schedules in breaks for workers to ensure that their well-being is well taken care of.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond our air and sea gateways, Mr Liang Eng Hwa raised the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore HSR project.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Such bilateral projects can only proceed if there are mutual interests and benefits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We remain open to discussing new proposals with Malaysia in good faith, starting from a clean slate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Dennis Tan, Mr Edward Chia and Ms Poh Li San have highlighted the importance of greening our aviation and maritime sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For aviation, our Sustainable Air Hub Blueprint sets the direction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Sustainability aviation fuel will remain our primary lever for cutting emissions across the bulk of our air traffic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For maritime, the MPA is working closely with the industry to prepare for a multi-fuel future, by investing in infrastructure, developing technical standards and licensing frameworks to ensure that we can handle these fuels safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These efforts reflect our commitment to position our port to meet the evolving needs of international shipping as it decarbonises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa raised suggestions to support the electrification of heavy vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to monitor take-up and see how best to achieve our electrification targets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also continue to study new EV technologies adapted around the world, including smart charging technologies to better optimise the grid as well as battery energy storage solutions to manage grid capacity constraints during peak hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Poh Li San and Dr Neo Kok Beng have highlighted the opportunities in electric and hybrid-electric aircraft for short-haul routes and drones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I have extensively addressed this topic in my response speech during the Adjournment Motion on “Low Altitude-Economy: Building the Flying Car, Air Tourism and Drone Logistics Industry” during the 8 April Parliamentary Sitting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will be ambitious but pragmatic, and keep our options open.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There is potential for Singapore to go further as a centre of excellence for research into cleaner and greener aircraft, working with partners, such as the Agency for Science, Technology and Research and our IHLs, with funding set under RIE2030.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will study the Member's proposal carefully and work with industry partners to take it forward where it plays to our strengths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On drones, they are used across Singapore for a wide variety of functions, from ship-to-shore deliveries at our port to inspections of our rail and road infrastructure and high-rise cleaning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is how Singapore stays relevant and secures our competitiveness in an uncertain world.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: My transport GPC colleagues, Mr Edward Chia, Ms Yeo Wan Ling, Ms Poh Li San, Mr Jackson Lam, Mr Liang Eng Wah, Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Sharael Taha, have taken turns to explain the different tenets of the Motion statement and together with other hon Members of this House, including Dr Choo Pei Ling, Ms Gho Sze Kee, Ms Lee Hui Ying, Ms Valerie Lee, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Dr Wan Rizal, Mr Lee Hong Chuang and Dr Hamid Razak, put forth many thoughtful recommendations for the Government's consideration.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Many thanks to my PAP Parliamentary colleagues for working on this debate and for making these recommendations.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I also sincerely appreciate the interest and support from the WP – Mr Dennis Tan, Ms He Ting Ru, Mr Fadli Fawzi, Mr Kenneth Tiong, Mr Gerald Giam and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim – as well as Nominated MPs, Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari and Dr Neo Kok Beng.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Past Sittings have seen colleagues from both sides of the aisle raising questions and putting forth suggestions on issues pertaining to Singapore's logistics, maritime and aviation sectors.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I am heartened, therefore, that we have such a robust debate on this Motion today and most of all, I am heartened by the support from both sides of this House that the transport GPC has put forth.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: We all want to do good for Singaporeans, creating good job opportunities for them by advancing Singapore's long-term economic interest.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: And we all agree that Singapore, being a global logistics, maritime and aviation hub, is key to that goal.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Across this debate, several threads ran consistently through nearly every speech, regardless of who from which party was speaking.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Members agreed that we are facing an increasingly turbulent world and geopolitics.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: That shared recognition makes the rule of law and our ability to work closely with one another all the more important.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I am heartened in this regard by hon Member from the WP, Ms He Ting Ru's point that Singapore should not be an instrument of other countries' strategic goals.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I agree, and this is why this Motion matters.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: We do not stay independent by standing alone.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: We stay independent by standing strong enough so that no one else's strategy needs to become ours.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: On frontier technology, Members spoke of AI, AVs, digital twins and smart hubs.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: On international cooperation and infrastructure, Members return again and again to the idea that our infrastructure is only as valuable as the trust the world places in it, whether framed through ASEAN chairmanship priorities, regional connectivity with Johor and the Riau Islands or Singapore's role in shaping international rules, rather than merely following them.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I am also encouraged that there was support from some Members from both sides to export Singapore innovations and systems to other countries.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Doing so would help set new standards and drive interoperability to drive greater flows of goods, people, information and value seamlessly, yet also strengthen Singapore's standing in the region and in the world.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Our tripartite model must therefore continue to prevail.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: So, yes, we need to embrace technology, but we must not vibe code the humans out of a job.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Rather to make sure that every job that we redesign or create beat to the rhythm of real heart beats.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: One Member, hon Mr Fadli Fawzi, had understandably raised his concerns about day-to-day public transport matters.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: As mentioned in my opening, day-to-day land transport issues remain important and a priority to the transport GPC and indeed, for the entire Government.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: We had and we will continue to discuss these issues in and out of this House, but I would like to reiterate that today's Motion was deliberately framed to look further out at the strategic long-term question of how Singapore secures our place in the world through global connectivity and logistics, maritime and aviation.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: The Member would agree that we need these connections for our food, medicine and other essential supplies to enter Singapore, so that Singaporeans can access them easily.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Attending to the everyday public transport issues and building for Singapore's global connectivity and future are not competing priorities.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: We agree that the world has grown more uncertain and that Singapore's independence must be built, not assumed.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It is Singapore's direction spoken with one voice across party lines and with that, thank you all.
